sources.title: HTTP semantics
sources.independent_observation: Strong ETags are the default; W/ marks weakness. If-None-Match uses weak comparison. Equal strong tags on the same resource have conditional evidential value; a 304 does not execute local extraction or establish note applicability.
sources.operation: Independent primary context inspection; source/code/test reading only.
sources.applicability: Only the stated generic proposal behavior and scoped historical example; no target-system validation.

sources.title: HTTP caching
sources.independent_observation: Vary matching, conditional request construction, intermediary responses and metadata updates differ from release identity. Disconnected stale reuse remains directive-limited; retained historical evidence is distinct from an HTTP response cache.
sources.operation: Independent primary context inspection; source/code/test reading only.

sources.title: Web Annotation
sources.independent_observation: Quotes require normalized Unicode code points; positions are end-exclusive and brittle. Multiple quote matches remain multiple matches. State precedes selector processing. Local extraction/version binding and human-reviewed candidates fit these limits.
sources.operation: Independent primary context inspection; source/code/test reading only.
sources.applicability: Only the stated generic proposal behavior and scoped historical example; no target-system validation.

sources.title: PROV-O
sources.reviewed_locator: wasRevisionOf, wasQuotedFrom, specializationOf, alternateOf; expanded definitions
sources.independent_observation: Revision entails substantial retained content; quotation, specialization and alternate entities express different relationships. A URL redirect alone does not establish these relationships. Relational use of the vocabulary need not adopt an RDF runtime.
sources.operation: Independent primary context inspection; source/code/test reading only.
sources.applicability: Only the stated generic proposal behavior and scoped historical example; no target-system validation.

sources.title: Git data model
sources.independent_observation: Object content is immutable while retained; refs can move. Repository, full object/commit and path are useful pins. A commit or version label is not itself publisher authentication or product compatibility evidence.
sources.operation: Independent primary context inspection; source/code/test reading only.

sources.title: Memento
sources.independent_observation: Datetime negotiation and TimeMaps support recovery where covered. Requested and selected dates can differ; replay may transform bytes. Archive time is not a product release. Both proposals keep archive provenance separate.

sources.independent_observation: Verified #7109 adds method preservation for 308. The proposed checker uses GET, so no material decision turns on omitted POST behavior. No verified erratum found reverses the assessed validator semantics.

sources.title: HTTP caching errata
sources.independent_observation: Reported #9185 proposes allowing strong-ETag identification despite selecting-header mismatch. It is not a verified normative amendment. The finals use a conservative same-variant policy; neither may be treated as a complete protocol extension design.

sources.independent_observation: The design discussion explains restricting update scope to avoid Last-Modified-driven cross-variant corruption. It contextualizes RFC 9111 and reported erratum #9185 without turning an unresolved proposal into current authority.

sources.title: Prior HTTP caching edition
sources.independent_observation: The older update-selection formulation is historical context, not the governing edition. A general statement that all validation is useless would be wrong; the finals instead distinguish it from local selector and digest execution.

sources.title: Hash names
sources.independent_observation: Name-data integrity depends on algorithm, input boundary and checking. Byte naming does not confer publisher identity or confidentiality. No ni-URI adoption is required by the proposal.
